posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Newest DCG Hologram.

8" by 10"

I know, a lot to be desired in the coating and the rushed glue job. I made the dreaded mistake of mixing the fast cure epoxy before I scraped the edge and would you know it, I didn't have enough epoxy to mix up another batch so I tried using is sticky, stringy and half set. 

but... Nice and bright, large format with no greenies (or very small and minimally - under chin) and I tried to make the light much brighter at his face and chest region which seemed to turn out as expected. My fist 8x10. No matter how bad, I will treasure it.

![Image](http://www.holograms3d.com/PhotoGal/General/Jesus8x10.JPG)

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Hi John,

Thank you for the picture! No greenies! I do see some places that have dropped out however. Is this from improper drying? I have seen this in DCG before.

I assume the epoxy casued the dark features on the upper side.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: If you mean the drop out at the hands and feet/legs, no. I planned it that way. I was kind of shooting for an emanation of light from his spirit, which I feel is located at the heart. Thus I wanted the region close to his heart to be the brightest with dimming moving outward. I used a lower power objective to keep the light in a tighter circle. If I remember correctly, the bottom corners of the plate were about 1/10 the energy then the area over the heart.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: No, actually I was talking about the area above the left hand (from my point of view) in the black section.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: nice job john. what was your exposure time?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Colin, sorry. Yes I see. It seems to be streaks but I am not sure what it is. Could be the way I brought it out of one of the alcohols or the way I put it in the fixer. Or maybe diffaction lines from the edge of my baffle but I didn't notice it when it was set up. I will look at the holo in laser light to check and look closer at the emulsion.

Dave, the exposure was 60 seconds. Laser was putting out 350mw in 488. Beam was expanded to about 12-14 inches in diameter (pretty hot in center and center was over chest). I cannot say what power was actually hitting the plate as I use an old Metrologic light meter that was made for 632nm. It is good for relative measurement since I know about what I need from experience with this meter, but I am sure its readings are not absolute.
